headline: Elon Musk said Tesla's Austin robotaxis will run an hour later at night while the company works on spotting pets in the dark.
score_reason: Small operational change plus a candid admission about night vision; rests on Musk's posts as reported by one outlet.
importance_line: Austin riders get robotaxi service until 11 p.m., and pet owners and pedestrians learn that low-light detection is still being solved on a camera-only system already under a federal investigation, though the claims are Musk's own.
summary: Business Insider reports that Elon Musk said on 3 Oct 2026 that Tesla is extending its Austin robotaxi hours from 10 p.m. to 11 p.m., and that the main problem his team is solving is avoiding pets that are hard to see at night, in his words "grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark". Tesla's robotaxis rely on cameras rather than laser-based lidar, and the US safety regulator NHTSA is already investigating whether that camera system spots hazards well enough in poor visibility.
notes: machine_action true: robotaxis operating in service at night.
